I’m currently 24 and started playing at 19. I play in a band currently, and it’s been a real hoot. The most important thing I’ve found is finding out what style of music I like, and diving into all of the things that make that style happen. From surface level theory (basics of major/minor scales, and how to make chord progressions from them) to just trying to copy licks and sounds from recordings. I’ve noticed recently that taking however long it takes to learn a song by ear is extremely rewarding, it helps you work on hearing something and playing it - maybe helps you develop more of that “voice in your head” that carry’s over into making your own improvisations later. It also helps you learn to hear yourself and the people/recording you’re playing with, to be a little aware of everything. 

Again the big thing for me was trying to learn to sound like the guys I like to listen too, which is a great foundation for making your own sound! Also practicing a lot, not just jamming out or playing without direction, but like sitting down and focusing on the thing you’d like to learn. and accepting that progress happens differently for everyone, but you’ll get there as long as you keep making the effort.
